from setuptools import setup, find_packages

setup(
    name="files-context-education",
    version="0.1.0",
    description="Meltano Cloud industry context for education: datasets for AI assistants and analysts.",
    packages=find_packages(),
    # bundle/ is copied verbatim into the workspace repository; ship every file under it
    include_package_data=True,
)

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Education: data model"
questions: What are the core entities of education data, and at what grain should each be modelled?
description: |
  The entities most education data reduces to, with the grain and key of each. Use it to map raw
  source tables onto a consistent model. Names are suggestions; keep the organisation's own terms
  where they already exist (pupil, student, learner).

  | Entity | Grain (one row per…) | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `learner` (pupil, student) | person | Internal ID plus statutory IDs (the UPN for pupils in England, the ULN in FE, a HUSID in UK HE). Never key on name and date of birth |
  | `academic_period` | academic year, term or semester | Start and end dates, census dates. The reporting calendar |
  | `course` (programme, qualification) | course version | Qualification aim, level, credits, duration. Versioned: curricula change between years |
  | `module` (unit, class, section) | module instance per period | The thing taught and timetabled. Sections in US terminology |
  | `enrolment` | learner per course per period | Start date, expected and actual end date, mode (full or part time), status, completion outcome |
  | `module_enrolment` | learner per module instance | Credits attempted and earned, final mark and grade |
  | `session` (timetabled event) | session | Date, time, room, staff member, module |
  | `attendance_mark` | learner per session | Present, late, authorised or unauthorised absence. Schools record morning and afternoon sessions |
  | `assessment_result` | learner per assessment | Assessment, mark, grade, attempt number, whether it was a resit |
  | `award` | award conferred | Qualification, classification or grade, date |
  | `application` | application | Course applied for, cycle, offer, decision, firm or insurance choice, entry |
  | `staff` | staff member | Role, contract, FTE. Linked to sessions and modules taught |
  | `lms_activity` | learner per course site per day | Logins, page views, submissions. Aggregate from raw event logs |
  | `fee_invoice` / `funding` | invoice or funding line | Tuition fees, sponsor, bursaries, government funding by learner |

  ## Relationships

  - A **learner** has one or more **enrolments** on **courses**, each in an **academic period**.
  - An enrolment has **module enrolments**, and each module instance has **sessions** and
    **assessments**.
  - **Attendance marks** link a learner to a session; **results** link a learner to an assessment.
  - An **application** becomes an **enrolment** when the applicant accepts and registers.

  ## Status and history

  Enrolment status changes (applied → enrolled → withdrawn, transferred, completed), and statutory
  reports count it as at fixed census dates. Snapshot enrolments at each census date, and keep the
  history of status changes with their effective dates.

  #education #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Education: modelling it in dbt"
questions: How should raw education data be modelled in dbt so that it reconciles?
description: |
  Conventions for building dbt models on raw education data. They apply on top of the workspace's
  usual dbt layout: staging, then intermediate, then marts.

  ## Academic calendar

  - **Build a calendar dimension** (`dim_academic_calendar`) with academic year, term or semester,
    teaching weeks, holidays and census dates per day. Do not derive the academic year from the
    calendar year with a fixed month: it differs by organisation and sometimes by course.
  - Name academic years consistently (for example `2025/26`) and store the start and end dates.
  - Count **possible sessions** from the timetable and the calendar, not from attendance marks alone:
    a missing mark is not the same as an absence.

  ## Learners and enrolments

  - **Resolve learner identity once.** The SIS, LMS, admissions and exams systems each have their own
    IDs. Build a `dim_learner` with a crosswalk to each source ID and the statutory IDs, and test it
    is one-to-one.
  - **Model at enrolment grain.** Retention and achievement are counted per enrolment; counting per
    learner double-counts or loses learners on more than one course.
  - **Treat withdrawals and transfers explicitly.** Keep the withdrawal date and reason, and whether a
    transfer created a new enrolment. Most retention definitions depend on them.
  - **Snapshot at census dates.** Use dbt snapshots or the source's history so statutory counts can
    be reproduced as at each census date.

  ## Results

  - Keep marks and grades in separate columns. Grades are ordered categories (A*–G, 9–1, first to
    third): map them to an ordinal value in a seed rather than sorting text.
  - Keep **every attempt** and flag the one that counts (best, latest or capped resit, depending on
    the regulations).

  ## LMS and event data

  - LMS logs are high volume. Load them incrementally and aggregate to learner per course per day or
    week in an intermediate model; marts should not scan raw events.
  - Map LMS course sites to SIS module instances with an explicit mapping table: names and codes
    rarely match exactly.

  ## Tests

  Add these beside the usual `unique` and `not_null` tests:

  - **Statutory agreement:** enrolment and learner counts agree with the latest submitted return (the
    school census, ILR or HESA return) for the same period and definition.
  - **Attendance:** each learner has at most one mark per session; possible sessions ≥ attended.
  - **Date logic:** enrolment end date ≥ start date; results fall within the enrolment.
  - **Accepted values** on attendance codes, enrolment statuses and grade scales.
  - **Freshness** on attendance sources, which are used daily for safeguarding follow-up.

  ## Naming

  - Prefix models by layer (`stg_`, `int_`, `fct_`, `dim_`), and name facts for their grain:
    `fct_enrolments`, `fct_attendance_marks`, `fct_assessment_results`, `fct_applications`.

  ## Sensitive columns

  Tag personal and special category columns (ethnicity, SEN or disability, free school meals,
  safeguarding flags) in the model YAML, for example `meta: {pii: true, special_category: true}`,
  and keep them out of marts that do not need them. See *Education: handling the data*.

  #education #organisation-context

# files-context-education

A Meltano [file bundle](https://docs.meltano.com/concepts/plugins/#file-bundles) of **industry
context for education**. Meltano Cloud adds it to a workspace whose organisation's industry
is Education.

The bundle holds datasets with no query. Each one is a written briefing: the segments and source
systems of the industry, its core entities, the metrics it runs on, how to model its data in dbt,
and how to handle its data. They are written for an AI assistant (or an analyst) working in the
workspace, for example one building dbt models on raw education data.

```
analyze/datasets/education/
  overview.yml
  data-model.yml
  metrics.yml
  dbt-modelling.yml
  data-handling.yml
```

## Organisation knowledge: `#organisation-context`

Every dataset here is tagged `#organisation-context`, the tag of an organisation's knowledge in Meltano
Cloud. The `get_organisation_knowledge` MCP tool returns the full text of every dataset with it, for an
AI assistant to read before it models, transforms or queries the workspace's data. In the repository,
`grep -rl '#organisation-context' analyze/datasets` finds the same set. Tag a dataset of your own the
same way to add it.

## Install

Meltano Cloud installs it when Education is chosen as the workspace's industry, in the
setup wizard or with the `set_organisation_context` MCP tool.

In a Meltano project of your own, save this definition to a file outside the project, for example
`/tmp/files-context-education.yml`:

```yaml
name: files-context-education
namespace: files_context_education
variant: matatika
pip_url: git+https://github.com/meltano/files-context-education.git@v0.1.0
update:
  '*.yml': true
```

then add the bundle from the project directory. `meltano add` writes the datasets; a plain
`meltano install` does not:

```sh
meltano add --plugin-type files files-context-education --from-ref /tmp/files-context-education.yml
```

`update: '*.yml': true` lets `meltano upgrade files` refresh the datasets from a newer version.

## Release

Tag a version (`git tag -a v0.1.0 -m v0.1.0 && git push --tags`) and bump the `pip_url` ref in the
Meltano Cloud registry definition (`plugins/files/files-context-education--matatika.yml`).

These datasets are general industry context, not legal, regulatory or safeguarding advice.

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Education: industry overview"
questions: What does an education organisation's data look like, and where does it come from?
description: |
  Industry context for this workspace, for the people and AI assistants working in it. It has no
  query: it is a briefing to read before modelling or analysing this organisation's data.

  ## Segments

  Education covers organisations that teach, assess and support learners. The segments differ in
  which entities and metrics matter most:

  - **Schools and school groups (K-12):** maintained schools, academy trusts, independent schools and
    US school districts. Pupils, classes, attendance, behaviour, assessments and staffing drive the
    data.
  - **Further education and colleges:** vocational and adult learning, apprenticeships. Learners,
    enrolments on courses, funding returns, attendance, retention and achievement drive the data.
  - **Higher education:** universities. Applicants, students, programmes and modules, credits,
    progression, completion, outcomes, research income and student finance drive the data.
  - **Training providers and apprenticeships:** employer-funded and government-funded training.
    Learners, employers, learning plans, off-the-job hours and end-point assessment drive the data.
  - **EdTech and online learning:** platforms and course providers. Users, enrolments, content
    engagement, completion and subscriptions drive the data.

  ## Typical source systems

  | System | Examples | What it holds |
  |---|---|---|
  | Student information / management (SIS, MIS) | Schools: Arbor, Bromcom, SIMS, PowerSchool, Infinite Campus. FE and HE: Ellucian Banner, Tribal SITS:Vision, Tribal ebs, Unit4 Student Management, Workday Student | Learners, enrolments, timetables, attendance, assessment results, awards |
  | Learning management (LMS / VLE) | Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard Learn, D2L Brightspace, Google Classroom | Course sites, activity, submissions, grades |
  | Admissions and recruitment | UCAS feeds, Common App, Slate, Salesforce Education Cloud | Applicants, applications, offers, conversions |
  | Assessment and exams | Exam board results files, e-assessment platforms, Turnitin | Entries, marks, grades, similarity reports |
  | Safeguarding and wellbeing | CPOMS, MyConcern | Concerns, incidents, actions (highly sensitive) |
  | Timetabling and attendance | The SIS's own modules, Celcat, Scientia | Sessions, rooms, registers |
  | HR and finance | Workday, Unit4, Agresso, Sage, iTrent, Oracle | Staff, contracts, payroll, budgets |
  | Apprenticeship and FE tracking | OneFile, Aptem, Bud | Learning plans, evidence, off-the-job hours, progress reviews |

  ## What makes the data different

  - **It runs on the academic year, not the calendar year.** Terms, semesters and academic years
    (for example August to July in England) define reporting periods, and statutory returns use
    fixed census dates.
  - **Enrolment is the core fact, not the person.** A learner can be on several courses, change
    course, withdraw and re-enrol. Retention, achievement and funding are counted per enrolment.
  - **Statutory returns set the definitions.** Government returns (the school census, the ILR in FE,
    the HESA Data Futures return in UK HE, IPEDS in US HE) define many metrics. Match their rules
    where the organisation reports against them.
  - **The data is about children and young people.** It includes special category and safeguarding
    data and needs strict access control. See *Education: handling the data*.

  Related datasets: *data model*, *metrics*, *modelling it in dbt*, *handling the data*.

  #education #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Education: key metrics"
questions: Which metrics does an education organisation run on, and how is each calculated?
description: |
  Standard definitions of the metrics education organisations report. Confirm each one with the
  data or quality team before building it: statutory definitions differ by country, phase and year,
  and organisations differ on start-date cut-offs and exclusions.

  ## Attendance

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Attendance rate | Sessions attended ÷ possible sessions. Schools in England count morning and afternoon sessions |
  | Absence rate | Sessions missed ÷ possible sessions, split into authorised and unauthorised |
  | Persistent absence | Learners missing 10% or more of possible sessions ÷ all learners (the England schools definition) |
  | Class attendance (HE/FE) | Sessions attended ÷ sessions timetabled, per module or course |

  ## Recruitment

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Applications | Count of applications in a cycle, by course and entry route |
  | Offer rate | Offers made ÷ applications decided |
  | Conversion (yield) | Enrolled learners ÷ offers made, or ÷ firm acceptances. State which |
  | Enrolment against target | Enrolled learners (or FTE) ÷ planned or funded numbers |

  ## Retention, progression and achievement

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Retention rate | Enrolments completed (not withdrawn) ÷ enrolments started. Exclude early leavers within the funding qualifying period where the statutory measure does |
  | Achievement rate (FE) | Enrolments achieved ÷ enrolments that ended in the year. Follows the qualification achievement rate (QAR) rules where reported |
  | Continuation (HE) | Entrants still studying or qualified a set period after starting ÷ entrants |
  | Progression | Learners who move to the next year or level ÷ learners eligible |
  | Completion (graduation) rate | Learners who completed their award within a set time (for example 150% of normal time in IPEDS) ÷ the starting cohort |
  | Pass rate | Assessments passed ÷ assessments attempted. Say whether resits count |

  ## Attainment

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | Grade distribution | Share of results at each grade, by subject and cohort |
  | Value added (progress) | Actual result − result expected from prior attainment (for example Progress 8 for schools in England) |
  | Good honours | First and upper second class degrees ÷ classified degrees (UK HE) |
  | Attainment gap | Difference in a measure between groups (for example disadvantaged and other learners) |

  ## Engagement and operations

  | Metric | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | LMS engagement | Active learners on a course site in a week ÷ enrolled learners. Define "active" explicitly |
  | Assignment submission rate | Submissions on time ÷ submissions due |
  | Student-to-staff ratio | Learner FTE ÷ teaching staff FTE |
  | Room utilisation | Hours rooms are used ÷ hours available, weighted by occupancy where measured |

  #education #organisation-context

version: datasets/v0.3
title: "Education: handling the data"
questions: What care does education data need in the warehouse?
description: |
  Education data is about learners, many of them children, and includes some of the most sensitive
  personal data an organisation can hold. These are general practices for a warehouse holding it.
  They are not legal, compliance or safeguarding advice: the organisation's data protection officer
  and designated safeguarding lead decide what applies to it.

  ## Classify the data

  | Class | Examples | Handling |
  |---|---|---|
  | Safeguarding and child protection | Concerns, referrals, looked-after status, case notes | **Do not load it into the shared warehouse.** If it must be analysed, keep it in a separate, tightly restricted area with counts only in shared marts |
  | Special category data | Ethnicity, health, disability and SEN, religion | Restrict access. Use only in aggregate for equality and funding reporting |
  | Indicators of disadvantage | Free school meals, pupil premium, household income, bursaries | Restrict access and report only in aggregate, with small-number suppression |
  | Personal data | Name, date of birth, address, contact details, parent and guardian details, photos | Restrict access, mask in non-production and in marts that do not need it |
  | Education records | Attendance, behaviour, results, exclusions | Restrict to staff with a legitimate educational interest |
  | Statutory identifiers | UPN, ULN, HUSID, student ID numbers | Mask or tokenise outside the models that need them |

  ## Practices

  - **Least privilege.** Separate raw, staging and mart schemas, and grant raw schemas only to the
    pipelines and the people who maintain them. In a group of schools, restrict each school's staff
    to their own school's learners.
  - **Mask by default.** Hash or mask learner identifiers in shared marts, and give unmasked access by
    role.
  - **Suppress small numbers.** Groups of a few learners can identify individuals. Suppress or round
    counts below an agreed threshold in any published or widely shared report.
  - **No production data in development** without masking.
  - **Retention.** Pupil records, exam results and student records have different retention periods
    (some long, for transcripts and awards). Agree them with the organisation, and model deletion and
    anonymisation explicitly.
  - **Data subject requests.** Under GDPR and UK GDPR learners and parents can ask for their data;
    under FERPA parents and eligible students can inspect and request amendment of education records.
    Know where each person's data lives.

  ## Rules to be aware of

  Which apply depends on the organisation's country and activities. Common ones:

  - **UK:** UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018; the ICO's Age Appropriate Design Code for online
    services likely to be used by children; the Department for Education's statutory returns and
    Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance; Office for Students conditions for HE providers.
  - **EU:** GDPR, including national rules on the age of consent for online services.
  - **US:** FERPA (education records), COPPA (online services for children under 13), PPRA, and state
    student privacy laws.
  - **Vendors:** LMS, EdTech and assessment providers process learner data on the organisation's
    behalf; check data processing agreements before loading data from them.

  #education #organisation-context
